column3: MCP-Universe: Benchmarking Large Language Models with Real-World Model Context Protocol Servers
column11: Leading LLMs including GPT-5 (43.72% success rate), Grok-4 (33.33%) and Claude-4.0-Sonnet (29.44%), plus enterprise agents such as Cursor against a standard ReAct framework, on 6 domains spanning 11 real-world MCP servers with 133 tools, using execution-based format, static and dynamic evaluators producing binary pass/fail task outcomes.
column12: To address this critical gap, we introduce MCP-Universe, the first comprehensive benchmark specifically designed to evaluate LLMs in realistic and hard tasks through interaction with real-world MCP servers. (Abstract)
column14: The only out_of_scope row in this batch, and the call is deliberate. MCP-Universe contains no adversary, no untrusted or poisoned content, and no non-adversarial context-corruption failure mode. It is a pure capability benchmark: task success rate on Google Maps, GitHub, Yahoo Finance, Blender, Playwright and Google Search MCP servers. The two challenges it advertises are the 'long-context challenge' (input tokens grow with interaction steps - a token-budget and capability observation, not a trust or corruption claim) and the 'unknown-tools challenge' (agents are unfamiliar with precise tool usage). That is exactly the brief's description of out_of_scope: studies agent capability and task performance while using 'context' and 'long-horizon' in another sense, here largely because 'Model Context Protocol' happens to contain the word context. Ruling 1 does NOT apply, because Ruling 1 requires the paper to frame itself around a context problem (saturation, rot, dilution, distraction) and then measure only capability; MCP-Universe never makes the context-integrity claim in the first place, so there is no claim/evaluation gap, just an out-of-scope paper. Registry has no entry for it and should not acquire one. If the lead disagrees and wants MCP-server benchmarks retained as infrastructure context, this flips to benchmark_or_dataset with belongs_in_corpus=yes and names_registry_technique=no.

Not coded as a CLAIM/EVALUATION MISMATCH because the paper never claims to address context saturation, dilution, noisy history or any context-degradation failure mode; its claims are about composability, reproducibility and task accuracy, and GAIA/HLE/AIME/GPQA measure exactly that. The failure it names is 'long-horizon cascading error' - the agent not knowing where it is, which actions are valid, and what they do - plus UI drift; the fix is to ADD curated knowledge (contexts, parameterized actions, workflows, tacit knowledge) rather than to resist or filter content that should not be trusted. There is no adversary, no injected or corrupted content, no retrieval contamination, and no context-degradation measurement; 'session-bound context' is simply the no-prior-knowledge baseline and the only context handling is routine accessibility-tree truncation. Evaluation is WebArena success rate only. Registry disagreement: registry lists 'defense: Environment Maps (Contexts/Actions/Workflows/Tacit Knowledge)' but there is no attacker and no untrustworthy-context failure mode; recommend dropping from the corpus. technique_name left blank per the out_of_scope rule; the paper calls it Environment Maps. column3: MEMORA: Embodied Action Memory from Egocentric Videos for Reasoning and Planning

'Memory' and 'long-horizon' are used in the embodied-experience sense, not the untrustworthy-context sense: there is no adversary, no planted or corrupted content, and no context failure mode such as dilution, distraction or rot under study. If the corpus were to keep it, the secondary framing would be benchmark_or_dataset (MEMORA-Bench), not a defense. column3: REMAC: Self-Reflective and Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Collaboration for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation

column12: We propose a multi-robot collaborative planning framework with self-reflection and self-evolvement capabilities for long-horizon and multi-stage tasks. (Contributions)
column14: Out of scope under Ruling 3's definition: the paper is not about untrustworthy context at all. 'Long-horizon' here means multi-stage robot manipulation task capability, and the failures studied are physical planning errors (trying to open a microwave door while holding a carrot), not poisoned, stale or attacker-planted context. There is no adversary and no untrusted content anywhere in the pipeline; the self-reflection module checks physical pre- and post-conditions from camera images. REMAC is a capability/planning framework and its evaluation measures only success rate and execution efficiency. This is precisely the false-positive class the brief warns about ('long-horizon' used in another sense), not a CLAIM/EVALUATION MISMATCH case, because the paper never claims to address a context-integrity problem. Everything measured is task performance (game reward, win rate, supply centers) and sample efficiency. No prior registry entry.

column3: Agentic Test-Time Scaling for WebAgents
column11: WebArena-Lite (165 tasks, programmatic success checks) and 341 tasks sampled from GoBrowse (LLM-as-a-judge with Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct), averaged over three seeds. Baselines are ReAct at N=1, static majority/frequency voting at N=1/5/10/20, and uniform LLM Arbiter arbitration; metrics are task success rate and total prompt-plus-completion tokens per task. column12: CATTS improves performance on WebArena-Lite and GoBrowse by up to 9.1% over React while using up to 2.3× fewer tokens than uniform scaling, providing both efficiency gains and an interpretable decision rule. (Abstract)
column14: Registry entry is empty; no disagreement to record. Coded out_of_scope: this is an inference-time compute-allocation paper (Confidence-Aware Test-Time Scaling, CATTS: sample N candidate actions, cluster them semantically, use vote entropy and top-1/top-2 margin to decide whether to invoke an LLM arbiter). There is no untrusted content anywhere in the paper - no injection, no poisoned page, no corrupted memory, no noisy or adversarial observation. The failure mode studied is compounding per-step sampling error and wasted compute on easy steps, and the evaluation measures only task success rate and token cost. This is precisely the 'long-horizon in another sense' case named in the out_of_scope definition, so Ruling 1's mismatch marker does NOT apply: the paper never claims to address a context-trust problem, so there is no claim/evaluation gap, only a topic that sits outside the corpus. column3: OSWorld 2.0: Benchmarking Computer Use Agents on Long-Horizon Real-World Tasks
column11: 108 long-horizon computer-use workflows run against seven model families (Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Opus 4.7, Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5.5, Qwen 3.7-Plus, MiniMax M3, Kimi 2.6) at a 500-step budget, under batched and single tool-call settings and swept reasoning-effort levels. Metrics are binary task completion and partial score, plus cost, tool calls, output tokens and steps per task; best result is Claude Opus 4.8 at 20.6% binary / 54.8% partial. Comparison point is OSWorld 1.0 / OSWorld-Verified, where the same agents score 79-83%.
column12: These results show that current agents are still far from professional-level computer use: rather than stumbling on basic GUI control or coding, they lose track of constraints, miss information that arrives mid-task, guess rather than ask the user, and skip verification, struggling most when a task hinges on hidden state they must recover. (Abstract)
column14: Registry entry is empty; no disagreement to record. Coded out_of_scope under Ruling 3's definition rather than under 'proposes no technique': this is a capability benchmark for computer-use agents, and 'long-horizon' here means task length and tool-call count, not untrustworthy context. Verified by full-text grep: the only occurrences of injection/poison/adversarial/malicious in the whole document are (a) an AgentDojo citation in the reference list and (b) adversarial tests used to find evaluator loopholes during benchmark construction. The nearest thing to an in-scope phenomenon is the 'dynamic environment' challenge, where a new email arrives mid-task and the agent must re-plan, plus safety reports auditing destructive execution (an agent running pkill -f libreoffice and discarding the LibreOffice Document Recovery dialog, and credential leakage cases). Both are agent-safety and state-tracking issues under benign-but-changing input, not content the agent should not have trusted, so they do not pull the paper into the corpus. Flagging this for the lead as the closest out_of_scope call in my packet: if the SoK decides to cover non-adversarial mid-task information loss, this benchmark would become relevant.

column3: Inside the Scaffold: A Source-Code Taxonomy of Coding Agent Architectures
column11: No experiments on agent behavior. The study is a source-code reading of 13 open-source coding agent scaffolds at pinned commit hashes (OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, OpenHands, Cline, Aider, SWE-agent, mini-swe-agent, AutoCodeRover, Agentless, Prometheus, Moatless Tools, DARS-Agent), characterized across 12 taxonomy dimensions in three layers, with every claim anchored to file paths and line numbers. column12: Each agent is characterized across 12 dimensions organized into three layers: control architecture, tool and environment interface, and resource management. (Abstract)
column14: Registry entry is empty; no disagreement to record. Coded out_of_scope although it is a survey/taxonomy, because Ruling 3 keeps surveys only when they are about untrustworthy context, and this one is not. Verified by full-text grep: zero occurrences of prompt injection, poison, untrusted, malicious, adversarial or context rot anywhere in the document. Its 'context strategy' and 'context compaction' dimensions are purely engineering descriptions of how each scaffold truncates or summarizes a growing message history to fit a token budget (the paper reports seven distinct compaction strategies and treats compaction as an open design question), with no claim about degraded or untrustworthy content and no measurement of any failure mode. Potential marginal value to the SoK as a reference for how production agents actually manage context, which is why I note the compaction finding here, but on the screening criteria it does not belong in the corpus.

column3: CarePilot: A Multi-Agent Framework for Long-Horizon Computer Task Automation in Healthcare
column11: CareFlow, the authors' own human-annotated benchmark of long-horizon healthcare software workflows (medical annotation tools, DICOM viewers, EHR systems, laboratory information systems), plus an out-of-distribution OpenHospital set. column14: Registry entry is empty; no disagreement to record. There is no adversary, no injected or retrieved untrusted content, and no non-adversarial context-trust failure mode; the failure modes analyzed are action-mode confusions (issuing ZOOM instead of CLICK, CLICK instead of SEGMENT) and the evaluation measures only step-wise and task accuracy against VLM baselines. column3: Can LLM Agents Sustain Long-Horizon Organizational Dynamics?

column14: REGISTRY DISAGREEMENT: registry has 'defense: TaskWeave (Formulate-Partition-Diagnose-Align)'. There is no adversary and no untrustworthy context anywhere in the paper. TaskWeave is a hierarchical multi-agent simulation framework whose concern is sustaining organizational state (role consistency, intent propagation, dependency satisfaction) over a long simulated horizon - i.e. agent planning/coordination capability, with 'long-horizon' used in the organizational-simulation sense, which the brief lists explicitly under out_of_scope. Note this is a borderline call: an alternative reading is proposes_fix for long-horizon state degradation, and in that reading there would be NO claim/evaluation mismatch marker, because the evaluation measures the coherence failure directly (role-allocation KL divergence against a reference prior, plan-propagation completion across temporal layers) rather than only capability. column3: MetaSkill-Evolve: Recursive Self-Improvement of LLM Agents via Two-Timescale Meta-Skill Evolution

(Abstract)

OUT OF SCOPE: there is no adversary, no untrusted content, and no context-integrity failure mode anywhere in the paper - 'skill' here is curated reusable procedural knowledge the agent authors for itself, and the entire framing is capability optimisation on agentic task benchmarks. This is NOT the Ruling 1 mismatch case: the paper never frames itself around a context problem (no context rot, saturation, distraction or dilution claim), so there is no claim/evaluation gap to mark - the claim is capability and the measurement is capability. column3: MANTRA: Synthesizing SMT-Validated Compliance Benchmarks for Tool-Using LLM Agents
column11: Generation side: 285 synthesized tasks across 6 domains (operations, sneaky-sasquatch, cabin-safety, tau2-retail, tau2-airline, tau2-telecom; manuals 566-16,644 words, 13-148 tools), forward/backward SMT cross-validation yield over 5 refinement rounds with Z3 and GPT-5 for LLM calls, plus a feature comparison against ToolBench, tau/tau2-bench, IntellAgent, AgentOrca, SOP-Bench, AgentIF, MCP-Bench and Agent-Diff. Agent side: 6 LLM models via the Strands framework, 285 tasks x 5 runs, success rate and a failure-category breakdown of 10,895 failed checks (76% Missing-Required-Call and Missing-Anchor).
column12: To overcome these limitations, we present MANTRA, a framework for automatically synthesizing machine-checkable compliance benchmarks from natural-language manuals and tool schemas. (Abstract)
column14: No prior registry entry, and I do not think one is warranted. MANTRA is a benchmark-synthesis framework for PROCEDURAL COMPLIANCE: can an agent follow the rules in a trusted natural-language manual, checked deterministically over its tool-call trace with SMT. There is no adversary and no untrustworthy context: the manuals and tool schemas are the ground truth the agent is graded against, not content it should distrust, and the failure categories it names (Missing-Required-Call, Missing-Anchor) are capability/instruction-following failures, not context-poisoning failure modes. Ruling 3 keeps benchmarks in the corpus, but only benchmarks about untrustworthy context, which this is not. Borderline consideration recorded for the lead: the manuals run to 50+ pages, so one could argue long-manual compliance is a long-context phenomenon, but the paper never frames or measures it that way - it attributes failures to tool complexity, not context length or degradation.

column3: SAG-Agent: Enabling Long-Horizon Reasoning in Strategy Games via Dynamic Knowledge Graphs
column11: Two API-free GUI game environments, Civilization V and Slay the Spire, against state-of-the-art API-free GUI agents (CRADLE, Bottom-Up Agent); metrics are exploration efficiency, skill acquisition and in-game strategic progress.
column12: We evaluate SAG-Agent in two complex, open-ended GUI-based decision-making environments (Civilization V and Slay the Spire), demonstrating significant improvements in exploration efficiency and strategic depth over the state-of-the-art methods. (Abstract)
column14: No prior registry entry, and none warranted. SAG-Agent is an experience-driven memory/skill-library framework (State-Action Graph plus a hybrid intrinsic reward) for pixel-only GUI game agents. 'Long-horizon reasoning' here means multi-step planning and exploration efficiency in Civilization V and Slay the Spire - the out_of_scope sense named in the brief. The one failure mode it names, 'experience siloing' (retrieving the most visually similar past state and failing to generalise across functionally similar but visually different states), is a retrieval-myopia/capability problem, not untrustworthy context: nothing the agent reads is planted, stale, conflicting or misleading. Not a claim/evaluation mismatch, since the paper claims exploration efficiency and strategic depth and measures exactly those.

(Abstract)
column14: No prior registry entry; none warranted. RoadmapBench is a SWE-bench-style coding benchmark: can an agent implement a release's worth of features (median 3,700 lines over 51 files) from a trusted roadmap instruction. 'Long-horizon' is the capability sense the brief lists as out_of_scope, and nothing the agent reads is untrustworthy - the pipeline in fact works hard to BLOCK contaminating information (target-version code, test files, oracle patch and future branches are all withheld). The failure taxonomy in the appendix (missing implementation, wrong module export, agent trapped in a degenerate ls loop until budget exhaustion) is about capability and agent control flow, not about poisoned or misleading context. Not a claim/evaluation mismatch: the paper claims to measure long-horizon development capability and measures exactly that.

column3: Images in Sentences: Scaling Interleaved Instructions for Unified Visual Generation
column11: InterleaveBench (image consistency and text consistency scored by Doubao-Seed-1.6, broken down by 2-5 objects) against DreamOmni 2, Flux-Kontext, Qwen Image, BAGEL and proprietary models, plus a component ablation (Image First, w/o video-based data, w/ VAE feature).
column12: To address these challenges, we propose Images iN SEnTences (a.k.a, Inset), a unified generation model that seamlessly embeds images as native vocabulary within textual instructions. (Abstract)
column14: Multimodal image-generation paper. Not about untrustworthy context in any sense: 'interleaved instructions', 'long-range dependencies' and 'long-horizon sequences' refer to multi-image prompt structure and training data, and the evaluation measures generation fidelity only. No adversary, no failure-mode measurement. Registry entry was empty; out_of_scope is the correct coding.

column3: SEC-bench Pro: Can Language Models Solve Long-Horizon Software Security Tasks?
column11: 344 validated vulnerability instances across V8, SpiderMonkey and the Linux kernel; six frontier commercial and open-weight models and three coding agents (best: CODEX with GPT-5.5 at 58%; GLM-5 solves 13/344); PoCs graded by replay on vulnerable/fixed/latest images plus a proposed LLM-based judge compared with existing rule-based judges.
column12: In this paper, we present SEC-bench Pro, a benchmark that measures how well frontier models hunt real vulnerabilities by reproducing working PoC inputs from disclosed reports, where each task pairs a concrete bug with the specific instructions for triggering it. (Abstract)
column14: Security topic but not context poisoning. 'Long-horizon' here means a multi-step code-auditing capability task, not untrustworthy context: the agent is the attacker-analogue, reading a codebase it is asked to audit, and the measurement is PoC reproduction success. Nothing adversarial is planted in the agent's context and no non-adversarial context failure is studied. The only trust-adjacent detail is a prompt that forbids fabricated outputs and requires verbatim captured stderr to stop hallucinated reproductions, which is benchmark hygiene, not a context-poisoning contribution. Registry entry was empty; out_of_scope per the brief's 'uses long-horizon in another sense' clause.

column3: ANX: Protocol-First Design for AI Agent Interaction with a Supporting 3EX Decoupled Architecture
column11: A single form-filling task (job account registration) in Dockerized OpenClaw Agent with Qwen3.5-plus and GPT-4o, 30 repetitions per method; ANX compared against GUI-based automation (Playwright/Chromium) and an MCP-based skill on total tokens, task-incremental tokens, execution time and task accuracy
column12: To address these issues, we present ANX, an open, extensible, verifiable agent-native protocol and top-level framework integrating CLI, Skill, MCP, resolving pain points via protocol innovation, architectural optimization and tool supplementation. (Abstract)
column14: Agent interaction protocol/architecture paper (ANX protocol, 3EX decoupled architecture, ANXHub). Mentions security only as keeping sensitive data (passwords, financial info) out of the agent context and requiring human-only confirmation; there is no adversary, no untrusted-context failure mode, and no security evaluation. Evaluation measures token consumption and latency on one form-filling task. This is an efficiency/architecture paper using 'context' in the token-budget sense, so out_of_scope per Ruling 3 rather than a Ruling 1 mismatch (the paper is not framed around context saturation/rot/distraction). Registry entry was empty; no registry disagreement.

column3: MCP-Cosmos: World Model-Augmented Agents for Complex Task Execution in MCP Environments
column11: 24 curated 2- and 3-server MCP-Bench tasks (300+ trajectories, 12 task types), comparing ReAct baseline against ReAct-Plan-Exec and SPIRAL-Exec with world models gpt-oss-120b, claude-sonnet-4.6 and Arctic-AWM-4B; metrics Task Completion, Tool Selection, Planning Effectiveness, Overall Score and the proposed Execution Quality
column12: We conducted experiments using two strategies, namely ReAct and SPIRAL with 2 planning models and 3 representative world models over 20+ MCP-Bench tasks. (Abstract)
column14: World-model-augmented planning for MCP tool use (BYOWM architecture, Execution Quality metric). No adversary and no untrusted-context failure mode; 'horizon myopia' is a planning-foresight limitation, and the evaluation measures tool success rate, parameter accuracy and planning effectiveness. This is agent capability/planning work using 'context' in the MCP-protocol sense, so out_of_scope per the field definition rather than a Ruling 1 mismatch. Registry entry was empty; no disagreement.

column3: A Multi-Agent Framework for Zero-Dimensional Reduced-Order Model Planning
column11: Three case families: two real aircraft-engine secondary air system design cases (forward and inverse design), two IEEE power-distribution reconfiguration benchmarks (55.46% active power loss reduction on the IEEE 69-bus network), and two water-distribution network design benchmarks (90.45% cost reduction on the Two-Loop network); plus Z-GPSolver solve-time and pressure-accuracy comparison against a Newton solver
column12: The results show that our multi-agent system achieves superior task completion quality, obtaining the best performance in both forward and reverse design of air systems. (Abstract)
column14: Engineering-design multi-agent system (Z-COPA with SAGE ontology-driven RAG and MILP-Guided Navigation) for zero-dimensional reduced-order model planning of air systems, power grids and water networks. No adversary and no untrustworthy context: the only context-related remark is that the Structured State Stream 'reduces information-loss risks from long contexts' and avoids state drift, an incidental engineering note with no measurement attached. Evaluation is entirely task performance (optimization quality, success rate, wall-clock time, solver accuracy), so out_of_scope per the field definition - 'context' here is design-state plumbing, not untrusted input. Registry entry was empty.

column3: GPA: Learning GUI Process Automation from Demonstrations
column11: Pilot study of 16 desktop GUI tasks (simple, avg 10.8 demo steps; hard, avg 27.27 steps) covering email drafting, receipt download, flight search/booking, Google Calendar, Agentforce, reimbursement, SAP ERP forms and HR workflows, comparing GPA against the Gemini computer-use agent (gemini-3-pro) on success rate and wall-clock runtime
column12: In this work, we present GUI Process Automation (GPA), a system that combines the ease of demonstration-based learning with robust geometric matching. (Introduction)
column14: Demonstration-based GUI/RPA replay system with Sequential Monte Carlo localization and a readiness checker. Security and privacy are mentioned only as local execution avoiding screenshot upload; there is no adversary, no untrusted context, and the evaluation measures success rate and speed on productivity tasks. Out_of_scope: agent capability and reliability work, not untrustworthy context. Registry entry was empty.

column3: OrchMAS: Orchestrated Reasoning with Multi Collaborative Heterogeneous Scientific Expert Structured Agents
column11: Six QA benchmarks (2Wiki, HotpotQA, GSM8K, DAPO, MuSiQue, PopQA) scored by F1 and Exact Match, against baseline models, SFT, CoT prompting, GRPO training and MAS optimization methods OPRO, TextGrad and GEPA; also reported for in-distribution and OOD settings across scientific QA, mathematical reasoning and multi-domain QA
column12: To address these limitations, we propose a scientific domain oriented interactive two tier multi model orchestration framework. (Abstract)
column14: Multi-agent orchestration framework (OrchMAS) with RL-trained orchestrator for scientific reasoning. The introduction lists 'sensitivity to irrelevant information' as one of several single-LLM weaknesses, but the paper is framed around static prompts, rigid workflows and homogeneous model reliance - capability, not untrustworthy context - and every reported number is task accuracy (F1/EM) on QA and math benchmarks. Not a Ruling 1 mismatch because the paper never claims to address a context-poisoning or context-degradation failure mode; coded out_of_scope. Registry entry was empty.

column3: Planner Matters! An Efficient and Unbalanced Multi-agent Collaboration Framework for Long-horizon Planning
column11: WebVoyager (four domains; Amazon, Google Maps, Allrecipes used for the scaling ablation) plus benchmarks spanning web navigation, OS control and tool use, with Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B/32B, GPT-4o and Gemini-2.5-Pro backbones; metrics are task success rate, fitted scaling-law coefficients per component, and GRPO planner fine-tuning with VLM-as-judge trajectory rewards
column12: Execution and memory management require significantly less compute and model capacity to achieve competitive results. (Abstract)
column14: Compute-allocation study for planner/actor/memory-manager decomposition plus planner-centric RL. 'Long-horizon' here means multi-step task difficulty, and the memory manager is a capability component, not a defense against untrusted or degraded context; all measurement is task success rate. Out_of_scope per the explicit field note about 'long-horizon' used in another sense. Registry entry was empty.

column3: An Intent-Driven Task Graph Framework for Safe Long-Horizon Execution in Embodied Agents
column5: 2026 7th International Conference on Mechatronics Technology and Intelligent Manufacturing (ICMTIM)
column11: Custom long-horizon banking benchmark (Foreign Currency Exchange, Cash Deposit) on the Tianyi humanoid robot with Qwen3-VL-397B, against Direct LLM one-go prompting, a ReAct agent and ReAcTree; metrics Task Success Rate, Execution Progress at Failure, average execution time, average token consumption, Constraint Violation Rate, Guideline Alignment and Unverified Actions
column12: We propose an intent-driven task graph framework for safe and reliable long-horizon execution in embodied service agents. (Abstract)
column14: Neuro-symbolic embodied-agent architecture that bounds an LLM planner inside pre-validated task subgraphs. The hazard it defends against is the LLM's own hallucination and non-determinism in a safety-critical physical workflow, not content the agent should not trust; there is no adversary, no injected or stale context, and the shared state is ordinary dialogue memory. Out_of_scope. Worth noting the evaluation does measure safety directly (constraint violations, unverified actions, guideline alignment), so it is not a capability-only paper - it is simply about a different threat. Registry entry was empty.
